newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair solves China cargo problems.
newsitem.headline: Martinair solves China cargo problems.

text.p: Martinair Holland NV, the Dutch air freight and passenger charter airline, is confident it will be able to start its postponed China freighter service in November, a spokesman said.
Problems of local registration and banking details have been solved and the airline hopes to launch a twice-weekly full freighter service between Amsterdam and Guangzhou next month, he stated.

He told Reuters in a telephone interview that some "small details" have still to be resolved. He declined to specify a specific date for the start of the new service and denied market rumours that Martinair, 50 pct owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV had had a disagreement with its Chinese partner Southern China Airlines.
Last month the Dutch airline said it had had to postpone its planned October one launch of the service due to what it described as administrative problems in China.

Martinair aims to be the first European airline to offer an air cargo service to the People's Republic of China, following an agreement sealed earlier this year between the Netherlands and China. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
